newsitem.title: USA: Oxbow Power to build Costa Rican geothermal plant.
newsitem.headline: Oxbow Power to build Costa Rican geothermal plant.

text.p: Oxbow Power Corp said Tuesday it has been chosen by Costa Rica's national utility to build and operate for 15 years a 27.5 megawatt (MW) geothermal power station at the Miravalles facility in Guanacaste Province.

The Japanese trading company Marubeni Corp, Oxbow Power Services, Inc of Reno, Nevada, and a local, unnamed investor were also in the consortium chosen by Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad (ICE) to build the new plant.
Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
ICE will provide the steam needed to run the plant and buy the power it produces, Oxbow said in a statement. ICE has a one-year option to order a second 27.5 MW geothermal unit.
The project, called Miravalles 3, joins two other power units at the site with a combined 110 MW generating capacity.
Oxbow Power Corp, based in West Palm Beach, Florida, is an affiliate of the privately-owned energy and minerals conglomerate Oxbow Group.
